The bug is in `com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeFoldConstants.tryFoldArrayAccess(Node, Node, Node)`.

Why:
- The failing input is `[,10][0]`.
- Static inspection shows:
  - `current = left.getFirstChild();`
  - `elem = null;`
  - loop: `for (int i = 0; current != null && i < intIndex; i++) { elem = current; current = current.getNext(); }`
  - then: `if (elem == null) error(INDEX_OUT_OF_BOUNDS_ERROR, right);`

For `intIndex == 0`, the loop does not execute at all, so `elem` stays `null`, and the method incorrectly reports index out of bounds even though the array has an element at position 0 (an EMPTY node in this test case).

This is an off-by-one / wrong-element-selection bug:
- index 0 is always treated as out of bounds for non-empty array literals.
- more generally, the code is tracking the previously visited node in `elem` instead of selecting the node at the requested index.

The dynamic verification attempt was inconclusive due to debugger session loss, but the static evidence is strong and directly explains the observed failure.
